clue.text: Bird, male variety, sitting on egg — big one

indicators.note: a bird sitting on eggs covers them, so the male goose here wraps round the egg and the big one

parts.note: the male variety of goose is the gander
an egg is round, like the letter O
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, a big one

explanation.surface: A male bird of some kind is brooding on a large egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting on' is the container signal: a brooding bird covers its eggs, so the gander wraps round them. OS for outsize is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A goosander is a fish-eating diving duck, a kind of merganser.

clue.text: German composer with piano — it's making holes in the ground

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Boléro
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A German composer at the keyboard seems to be digging holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarries dug to extract stones and grit leave large holes in the ground.

clue.text: Skipped from the ring with gloves on

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
mitted means wearing mitts or gloves

explanation.surface: A boxer left out of the ring is still wearing gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out.

clue.text: Notice politician extemporise

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a notice
Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A politician is seen improvising a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak off the cuff without preparation is to improvise or extemporise.

clue.text: Stationed in peculiar terminal

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is posted to a strange airport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the end point of a journey, where travellers arrive.

clue.text: Manipulate set-up of yacht

explanation.definitionFit: To rig is to manipulate a result fraudulently; a yacht's rig is its arrangement of masts and sails.

clue.text: Explorer to retreat by taxi

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: to retreat is to go backwards, so the little word to is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An explorer goes back home in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian navigator who reached North America in 1497.

clue.text: Eye's not functioning properly we hear — keeps on running

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an adjective: something that keeps on running is unending

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an eye that is failing sees less

explanation.surface: An eye that isn't working properly keeps on watering.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unending and incessant never stops, so it keeps going on and on.

clue.text: Built unusual structure on tree top and first egg's then laid in it

definitions.text: Built unusual structure on tree top and first egg's then laid in it

indicators.note: the egg's letter is laid inside the structure already built, as eggs go into a nest
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of built are rearranged
the top of tree is its first letter
the first of egg's is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A small bird builds a nest at the top of a tree and lays its first egg in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' scrambles BUILT into BLUTI, 'top' takes T from tree, and 'laid in' slips E (first of egg's) inside; the whole clue also pictures the bird nesting, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a small common garden songbird building a nest high up and laying in it.

clue.text: River used by golfers

explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England; golfers rest the ball on small pegs before driving off.

clue.text: Heavenly body of the gazelle

explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is a moon of Uranus, and also the name of an Arabian gazelle.

clue.text: A guest in reception initially could provide proof of identity

definitions.text: A guest in reception initially could provide proof of identity

parts.words: A guest in reception initially could provide proof of identity
parts.note: a hotel guest at the front desk signs the register on arrival, and 'initially' hints at writing one's initials

explanation.surface: A hotel guest at the front desk is asked for identification.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's handwritten name, written on a register, confirms who they are.

clue.text: Explode the mines — blast the ruling body!

indicators.note: exploding scatters things, so the letters of the following words are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A protester calls for mines to be blown up to damage the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an exclamation but is part of the fodder with 'the mines'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the dominant group that holds power and authority in a society.

clue.text: The rest come, staggering for short distances

indicators.note: to stagger is to lurch about unsteadily, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The remaining runners come staggering in over short distances.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred metres is a fairly short length, and the metric unit of that size is plural here.

clue.text: First-class row about Egyptian deity taking part in cabaret

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first two pieces enclose the god
first picks the opening letter of the word class

parts.note: a line is a row
Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian sky god

explanation.surface: A top-class row breaks out about an Egyptian god appearing in a cabaret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First-class' looks like 'excellent'; it gives C, the first letter of class, which with LINE goes 'about' HORUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus line is a row of dancers, the kind of act performed in cabaret and musicals.

clue.text: Gap Dora jumps, getting pain in the foot

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dora leaps over a gap and hurts her foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Podagra is the medical name for gout in the foot, especially the big toe.

clue.text: Re-interpreting this musical direction, lads sing round

indicators.note: re-interpreting a piece means rendering it differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Some boys reinterpret a musical instruction while singing a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' looks like a type of song the lads sing; it is just O, added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is an instruction to slide quickly through a run of notes.

clue.text: Feline's beguiling, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: one beguiling others by deceit is a cheater

explanation.surface: A cat is said to be charming.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big spotted cat, the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Ends in the interim,oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something finishes during the interval, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' suggests taking odd letters; here it is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end points, such as the last stations on railway lines.

clue.text: Army unit signalling regrets

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
Morse code is a system of signalling with dots and dashes

explanation.surface: A military unit sends a message of apology.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep sorrow and contrition over what one has done.

clue.text: Octopi heading south steer around sturgeon

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
around here means turned about and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Octopuses swim south, steering around a big fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The osseter, or oscietra, is a species of sturgeon prized for its caviar.

clue.text: Vessel goes through forest, then locks

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so the ship sits within the forest

parts.note: a forest is full of trees
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship passes through a forest and then a set of canal locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' sounds like canal gates for a vessel; it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks and tresses are both words for long hair.

clue.text: Times printers read-out gives us the wrong meaning

indicators.note: a misread printout comes out muddled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper's printing run produces a garbled message.
explanation.definitionFit: To misconstrue is to understand or explain in a wrong sense.

clue.text: Resting place for fish

explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a bar where a bird roosts, and also a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Twin entry in thesaurus

indicators.note: an entry in a book is contained in it, so the answer lies within the word

explanation.surface: A word for twin is listed in the thesaurus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was the twin brother of Jacob.

clue.text: Drops around when one is working

definitions.text: Drops around when one is working

parts.words: Drops around when one is working
parts.note: reads like a visitor calling in during work hours, but describes a garden device scattering water droplets when switched on

explanation.surface: Someone always pops in while you are busy at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn device spreads droplets of water over the grass while it runs.

clue.text: On edge, make a mistake and drop a point

indicators.note: drop means leave out, so the compass letter is taken away

parts.note: to slip is to make a mistake
S is south, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A nervous player blunders and loses a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The rim or brim of a cup or jug is its edge.

clue.text: Sort of Irish sage

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wise person of a vaguely Irish kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is a Hindu holy man or seer.

clue.text: Rude sort of circle — it's rust, in the garden

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A rude circle of gardeners complains about rust.
explanation.definitionFit: Uredo is a stage of the fungal plant disease called rust.

clue.text: Has to step lively? Yes!

indicators.note: lively means bouncing about energetically, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they must hurry up, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at top speed, with the utmost haste and urgency.
